---
title: "Lab 6B: AI R Plot Review"
---

## Goal

Practice reviewing AI-generated R code that runs successfully but produces an
under-checked plot and an overconfident claim.

## Scenario

A student asks an LLM to show how vehicle weight affects fuel economy. The
generated script resembles
[week06-ai-plot-review.R](../code/r/week06-ai-plot-review.R).

## Part A: Run The Generated Script

1. Open and run the script without editing it.
2. Record the plot title and axis labels.
3. Identify the mapped variables.
4. State whether the code produces an error.
5. Explain why “the code runs” is not enough to accept the plot.

## Part B: Inspect The Data First

Add code that reports:

- object class;
- row count;
- variable names;
- missing values in `wt` and `mpg`;
- ranges of both variables;
- the number of rows represented in the built plot.

Turn at least three of those expectations into `stopifnot` checks.

## Part C: Repair The Figure

Revise the plot so that it includes:

1. axis labels with complete units;
2. a noncausal title;
3. a caption identifying the observations;
4. a point style that is readable without implying a nonexistent category;
5. a minimal theme or other restrained formatting choice.

## Part D: Audit The Claim

Complete the table.

| Weakness | Why it matters | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| Causal title |  |  |
| Missing units |  |  |
| Unidentified observations |  |  |
| No row or missingness checks |  |  |
| No limitation |  |  |

## Part E: Write A Defensible Interpretation

Write 4-6 sentences that:

- describe the direction of the association;
- identify the dataset and sample size;
- use the correct units;
- avoid causal language;
- mention one important limitation.

## Deliverable

Submit:

- the original generated claim;
- your repaired R script;
- the completed audit table;
- the repaired plot;
- the defensible interpretation;
- one sentence explaining why successful execution is weaker evidence than a
  reproducible, checked analysis.

## Exit Question

Complete this sentence:

> An AI-generated R visualization is not trustworthy until ...
